paper.title_en: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
paper.abstract_en: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($θ_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($τ_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $γ$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.
